scenario.task: We want to consolidate duplicated schema/tool plumbing between the Google GenAI and Vertex chat integrations without changing public behavior. Locate exactly six declarations: each integration’s structured-output wrapper and tool-binding method, plus each integration’s low-level provider-tool collection converter. Return their declaration locations in claims. In limitations, give a source-cited compatibility review of what can be shared and what must stay provider-specific, focusing on actual executable branches, schema transformations, accepted input/options, tool conversion/packing, and returned results/error behavior. Resolve any documentation/implementation disagreement using code. Do not implement the refactor. Relationships must be empty. Do not enumerate additional declarations in claims.

metadata.purpose: Known public pilot; exact declarations and separately blinded source-rubric review; two fresh sessions per arm

limitations: Investigation scope: DeepThought's snapshot declaration graph was consulted, and all six locations and lexical scopes were independently confirmed with Python ast. Behavioral conclusions below come from reading production source. No repository modules were executed, files changed, dependencies installed, builds run, or network answers sought. External LangChain parser/converter and Google SDK internals were not available in the selected source, so their internal validation, streaming behavior, and server acceptance are not independently established.

Preserve method signatures and executable routing. GenAI permits method positionally and defaults to 'json_schema'; both 'json_schema' and 'json_mode' enter its native JSON branch. Vertex makes method keyword-only, defaults to None, and enters native JSON generation only for method == 'json_mode'. Neither wrapper validates method against its annotation: every other value enters function calling. In particular, Vertex's documentation says 'json_schema' selects controlled generation, but its implementation sends that value through function calling. A shared implementation must preserve this behavior rather than follow the contradictory prose. Both wrappers discard strict without enforcing it and reject remaining kwargs with ValueError. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/chat_models.py:3606-3614,3717-3726,3765-3785; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/chat_models.py:2658-2665,2699-2703,2830-2838,2870-2893.

Native JSON branches share schema-kind selection and parser selection, but differ in schema generation and binding. Both accept recognized Pydantic classes, TypedDict classes, and dictionaries; unsupported types raise ValueError. Both use schema() for Pydantic v1, PydanticOutputParser for Pydantic classes, and JsonOutputParser for TypedDict/dict schemas. GenAI calls model_json_schema() for v2, while Vertex requests mode='serialization'. GenAI binds response_json_schema and application/json; Vertex binds response_schema and application/json. GenAI separately normalizes tracing schemas through convert_to_json_schema for Pydantic, TypedDict, and dictionaries containing title, while untitled dictionaries pass through; Vertex records its transformed provider schema directly. These provider and tracing policies must remain distinct. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/chat_models.py:3730-3764; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/chat_models.py:2838-2869.

Reference and nullable handling cannot be unified unchanged. GenAI's native wrapper passes its generated/raw schema onward without local reference expansion or nullable stripping; its comment attributes transformation to the SDK, which is not behavioral proof of SDK internals. Vertex explicitly calls replace_defs_in_schema and then _strip_nullable_anyof. The reference helper handles dictionary-valued children using '#/$defs/name' paths, drops $defs when processing definitions, leaves list-valued children untraversed, rejects malformed paths with ValueError, and asserts that referenced definitions exist as dictionaries. It has no cycle detection. Nullable stripping collapses exactly two-branch nullable anyOf properties and removes them from required; it does not remove every anyOf despite the wrapper's broad comment. It walks properties, items, and combiners and mutates its input in place. Because reference replacement can return a shallow copy and preserves lists, nested caller-owned schema data can also be mutated. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/chat_models.py:3754-3759; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/chat_models.py:2855-2867; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/_utils.py:292-388.

Request construction reinforces the provider boundary. GenAI prefers response_json_schema over response_schema, adds only truthy schemas, requires application/json, and stores the schema as response_json_schema. Vertex processes any non-None response_schema, accepts application/json or text/x.enum, and calls the external SDK's _convert_schema_dict_to_gapic. Sharing these paths wholesale would change empty-schema handling, accepted MIME types, conversion, and error behavior. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/chat_models.py:2963-3012; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/chat_models.py:2020-2035; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/chat_models.py:84-90.

Function-calling orchestration is substantially shareable with provider-specific schema/name and choice policies. Both determine a tool name, use PydanticToolsParser(first_tool_only=True) for recognized Pydantic schemas, and otherwise select JsonOutputKeyToolsParser(first_tool_only=True). Vertex explicitly limits that latter case to TypedDict/dict and raises ValueError for other types; GenAI's branch has no equivalent explicit restriction, although earlier name conversion can fail. Vertex always requests the named tool. GenAI requests it only when _supports_tool_choice is true, using profile['tool_choice'] with a default of true. Their name helpers also differ: GenAI extracts the first declaration through its converter/serializer and retries TypedDict conversion only on ValueError; Vertex extracts the first declaration through the GAPIC converter. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/chat_models.py:3765-3785,3873-3893; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/chat_models.py:2870-2893,3067-3069.

The runnable result/error composition can be shared. Both wrappers first try binding with ls_structured_output_format and catch any Exception to retry binding without that metadata; failures before the try or in the retry propagate. Without include_raw they return llm | parser, allowing parsing failures to propagate. With include_raw they run the model into raw and apply a parser fallback: success yields raw, parsed, and parsing_error=None; parser failure preserves raw, sets parsed=None, and records the exception under parsing_error. The fallback surrounds parsing, not the model call or wrapper construction. Dictionary tool results are selected through JsonOutputKeyToolsParser rather than explicitly wrapped into an args/name list. These sources establish composition and parser choice, not the external parsers' exact streaming guarantees. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/chat_models.py:3775-3794; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/chat_models.py:2883-2903.

bind_tools has a shareable conversion/fallback skeleton but different policy and fallback values. Both first attempt convert_to_openai_tool for every input and, on any Exception, reconvert the entire collection through the provider converter. GenAI serializes each returned google.genai Tool using tool_to_dict; Vertex wraps its single GAPIC Tool in a list. Both ultimately return self.bind(tools=formatted_tools, **kwargs), forwarding additional kwargs. Vertex rejects simultaneously truthy tool_choice and tool_config before conversion and forwards one via if/elif. GenAI permits both and forwards each independently. Both use truthiness, so explicit False and empty options are omitted at binding time. Fallback conversion errors propagate. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/chat_models.py:3796-3805,3861-3871; libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/_function_utils.py:382-397; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/chat_models.py:2905-2912,2929-2945.

Tool configuration must retain provider-specific validation and timing. GenAI checks conflicts during request preparation, validates dictionary configs into ToolConfig, rejects tool_choice together with a populated function_calling_config, and rejects a truthy choice without formatted tools. For built-in-only tools with no function names, it returns the existing config or None without converting the choice. For callable functions, its merge explicitly carries the generated function_calling_config and the supplied retrieval_config. Vertex bind_tools rejects any truthy choice/config pair; its request path prioritizes supplied tool_config, otherwise converts tool_choice even if the extracted names are empty. Its dictionary config formatter requires function_calling_config. The Vertex helper returns None for an already-instantiated imported vertexai ToolConfig rather than passing it through. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/chat_models.py:3174-3261; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/chat_models.py:2228-2239,2544-2549,2929-2934; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/functions_utils.py:462-473.

Tool-choice normalization overlaps but is not identical. Both support true/'any', 'auto', 'none', named-function strings, lists, and dictionaries containing mode or function_calling_config. GenAI additionally maps 'required' to ANY with all function names; Vertex treats 'required' as an ordinary named-function string. Vertex additionally recognizes the OpenAI-shaped {'type':'function','function':{'name':...}} choice dictionary, while GenAI's helper rejects that shape. They construct different SDK configuration types and expose different error messages. A common normalizer would need explicit provider policies to preserve these differences. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/_function_utils.py:695-768; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/functions_utils.py:459-526.

Collection converter contracts and packing differ fundamentally. GenAI returns list[types.Tool], warns and wraps non-Sequence inputs, preserves existing types.Tool objects directly, emits separate special-tool objects, and appends accumulated function declarations as one final Tool. Thus converted functions move after preexisting/special tools; an empty collection returns []. Vertex directly iterates its input and merges recognized content into one new gapic.Tool, including fields from vertexai.Tool._raw_tool; an empty collection returns an empty gapic.Tool. Vertex does not implement GenAI's non-Sequence wrapping. Request helpers retain these contracts: GenAI uses the returned list, while Vertex wraps its single converted Tool in a list. Both prioritize truthy tools over functions, but Vertex additionally logs when both are supplied. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/_function_utils.py:219-250,331-379; libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/chat_models.py:3137-3150; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/functions_utils.py:306-328,376-379; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/chat_models.py:2528-2542.

Built-in tool acceptance and conflict checks must stay provider-specific. GenAI recognizes google_search_retrieval, google_search, google_maps, code_execution, url_context, and computer_use. Only non-None special dictionary values count; more than one special kind raises ValueError. A selected special branch bypasses function_declarations in the same dictionary. computer_use additionally normalizes serialized or object-valued environment enums. Existing types.Tool objects bypass that dictionary check. A final check rejects multiple truthy google_search_retrieval tools but does not reject mixing one with functions. Vertex recognizes google_search_retrieval, google_search, retrieval, and code_execution and processes multiple recognized keys within the same dictionary. Its retrieval guard runs before each iteration and examines the accumulated result: retrieval followed by any further tool raises ValueError, whereas functions followed by retrieval can finish successfully. The error text therefore overstates a symmetric prohibition on mixing. Preserve these actual order-dependent branches. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/_function_utils.py:237-379; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/functions_utils.py:306-379.

Declaration-container validation is observably different. GenAI accepts any Sequence for a non-None function_declarations value despite saying 'list' in its error message; tuples therefore pass that check. A None value falls through to ordinary function-dictionary conversion. Vertex requires an actual list whenever the key is present, rejecting tuples and None. Both skip empty accepted containers. GenAI's annotation includes types.FunctionDeclaration, but its element dispatcher has no explicit pass-through branch for such instances; annotations alone do not establish support. Vertex explicitly converts vertexai.FunctionDeclaration using to_dict. Both have executable support for OpenAI function dictionaries, despite GenAI's older comment claiming that shape is not accepted. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/_function_utils.py:65-92,332-360,400-428; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/functions_utils.py:272-303,348-361.

Element normalization can share selected patterns, but not unrestricted acceptance or side effects. Both handle BaseTool, Pydantic classes, callables, and dictionaries, and both synthesize a required string __arg1 parameter when a BaseTool lacks args_schema. GenAI explicitly supports v1/v2 BaseTool schemas and raises NotImplementedError for other args_schema types; Vertex uses dictionary/attribute-based schema selection and requests serialization mode for v2. Vertex excludes annotated classes from callable conversion and routes them through convert_to_openai_tool, supporting TypedDict-like classes there. GenAI's low-level dispatcher instead sends remaining callables through the LangChain tool decorator. GenAI mutates function dictionaries by filling parameters and replacing parameters lacking truthy properties with {}; its naming fallback is name, title, then 'MISSING_NAME'. Vertex's dictionary path delegates normalization to convert_to_openai_tool and uses name/description directly in its GAPIC builder. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/_function_utils.py:205-215,400-493; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/functions_utils.py:184-303.

Tool parameter schema conversion is not equivalent to native response-schema handling and cannot be consolidated into one unchanged transformer. GenAI dereferences schemas, uses a fixed allowlist, and explicitly builds types.Schema with only a subset of those allowed fields; fields such as minimum, maximum, pattern, and format are not copied by that final builder. It omits ordinary property titles, supplies empty top-level required when absent, defaults untyped nested schemas to STRING, infers OBJECT for top-level property-only schemas, and may return None for a top-level schema without type/anyOf/properties. Its property helper preserves non-null unions as anyOf, but nullable unions select the last available non-null type and mark nullable; nested object required fields are reconstructed from absence of defaults. Vertex derives allowed fields from the protobuf schema, uppercases types, and constructs gapic.Schema through JSON. Its v1 path filters null union branches; its v2 path also removes nullable properties from required, collapses single surviving candidates, and retains multiple non-null candidates. Both truncate allOf to its first entry and warn about unsupported keys, but those similarities do not make their transformations interchangeable. Sources: libs/genai/langchain_google_genai/_function_utils.py:39-61,95-202,502-600,648-681; libs/vertexai/langchain_google_vertexai/functions_utils.py:62-181,238-269.

Refactor boundary inferred from the verified source: shared helpers could own strict/extra-argument handling, configurable parser selection, tracing-aware bind retry, include_raw composition, the OpenAI-conversion-first fallback skeleton, and the common BaseTool __arg1 shape. Provider adapters must retain signatures/defaults, method routing, schema generation/transformation, tracing schema policy, tool-name and choice support, option conflict timing, built-in dispatch, SDK object construction/serialization, packing/order, mutation, and error behavior. This boundary follows the executable similarities and differences cited above; it does not assume behavioral relationships from declaration-graph containment.
